newsitem.title: USA: Allstate expands urban homeowners insurance.
newsitem.headline: Allstate expands urban homeowners insurance.

text.p: The Allstate Insurance Co, the National Fair Housing Alliance, and the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development said Wednesday that they have resolved the fair housing administrative complaints filed by NFHA against Allstate.

As part of the agreement, Allstate said it has asked the NFHA to help expand its programs to promote insurance opportunities in all urban neighborhoods. NFHA will also consult with the company on sales training and testing for three years. The agreement was reached, said the company, following complaints filed by NFHA with HUD in 1994. Allstate denies those charges and HUD made no determination that the Fair Housing Act was violated. But to enhance the company's urban initiative, the company said it would, among other practices:

* Maintain age-of-dwelling and minimum-value underwriting guidelines that state dwelling age and minimum value are not used as eligibility requirements for replacement cost homeowners policies. The company will provide written notice of the opportunity to obtain additional coverage to all customers with a market value or select value policy.

* Utilize a homeowners inspection process based on an objective assessment of the physical characteristics of a home as a requirement for issuance of a "new business" replacement cost homeowners policy.

* Maintain for one year its existing underwriting policy in which decisions to decline coverage for homeowners policies are not based solely on information in credit reports or credit scoring of the insured.
The company said it will also expand its Neighborhood Partnership Program, in which Allstate and urban community groups work to address insurance issues.
